provenance.l: InSight EDL reconstruction (NASA) — entry 5,542 m/s at −12.57°, 605.6 kg, 2.65 m aeroshell; chute at 5.52 km areodetic (~8 km above the site); touchdown 349 s at 2.7 m/s. Cd·A estimated from the Phoenix-class aeroshell; backshell separation 1.1 km from the JPL press kit (pre-flight)
InSight EDL — NASA JPL mission overview

InSight EDL timeline as researched for pass 2 (docs/wip/2026-11-23-mars-landings-record.md): chute at T−2:57, heat shield T−2:42 (15 s later), legs T−2:32 (25 s after the chute), radar T−1:00 (about 2.4 km), backshell T−0:44 then 12 engines to 2.4 m/s; arrays open 16–32 min after landing (16 min stamped). The record puts the chute at about 11.1 km; the reconstruction above puts it 8.1 km over the site, which the profile keeps. The chute (11.8 m) and the 2.65 m aeroshell are Phoenix-class
